title: SCORM import not needed for Sarvo-Shala
content: SCORM import is NOT a must-have for Sarvo-Shala (Swayam). The app is a single-user offline-first Rust+Tauri desktop tutor that authors its own curated content (seed snippets + AI Socratic dialog, FSRS/BKT). SCORM is an LMS-interop standard for third-party courses (Articulate/Captivate); consuming it requires implementing a full SCORM Runtime API + manifest parser + SCO webview player + sequencing engine = a mini-LMS. Only reconsider if a requirement emerges to ingest external authoring-tool courses or integrate with an LMS/LTI. For content portability, prefer a native lightweight package format. Comparable local-first study apps (Cortex, LearnForge, OfflineU, TutorialVault) do not implement SCORM.

title: Research papers to improve image-qc algorithms (orientation, binarization, dedup, OCR, QC)
content:
Curated academic search (2026-08-01) for improving image-qc's core algorithms. Searched via RivalSearchMCP academic_search (OpenAlex/CrossRef/arXiv/PubMed/EuropePMC) since mcp__flare__search type=academic had a downed backend (circuit breaker on rivalsearch->uv) at the time.

## 1. Orientation detection (relevant to qc_oar CNN classifier + Tesseract OSD fallback in image_qc/core/ocr/oar_engine.py)
- Unnikrishnan & Smith 2009, "Combined script and page orientation estimation using the Tesseract OCR engine" — https://doi.org/10.1145/1577802.1577809 — the algorithm behind the OSD fallback itself; explains OSD's low-glyph failure mode that oar_engine.py already works around.
- Pal, Mitra, Chaudhuri, ICDAR 2001, "Multi-skew detection of Indian script documents" — https://doi.org/10.1109/icdar.2001.953801 — Indian-script-specific, closest analog to Tamil/Kannada court docs.
- Ramanan 2019, "A Hybrid Approach for Skew Detection and Correction in Multi-script Scanned Document" — https://doi.org/10.9734/ajrcos/2019/v4i230112 — classical Radon/Hough/Harris-corner comparison.
- Le, Thoma, Wechsler 1994, "Automated page orientation and skew angle detection for binary document images" — https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-3203(94)90068-x — classical baseline.

## 2. Binarization (Sauvola A/B testing — image_qc `img to-bw`, qc_admin ocr-dump)
- Sulaiman et al 2019, "Degraded Historical Document Binarization: A Review" — https://doi.org/10.3390/jimaging5040048 — best survey of Sauvola/Niblack/Otsu variants and failure modes.
- Xiong et al 2021, "An enhanced binarization framework for degraded historical document images" (H-DIBCO 2018 winner) — https://doi.org/10.1186/s13640-021-00556-4 — classical (background estimation + energy minimization, no NN) — fits tenet #2/#3 as next A/B candidate.
- Bataineh et al 2011, "An adaptive local binarization method based on a novel thresholding method and dynamic windows" — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patrec.2011.08.001 — direct Sauvola alternative, good A/B harness candidate.
- Shafait, Bukhari, Breuel, "Adaptive Binarization of Unconstrained Hand-Held Camera-Captured Document Images" — https://doi.org/10.3217/jucs-015-18-3343 — specifically documents Sauvola's sensitivity to k/window-size params — directly actionable for tuning the currently-shipped Sauvola method.
- U-Net-bin (Bezmaternykh et al 2019, DIBCO'17 winner CNN) and DeepOtsu (He & Schomaker 2019) — only worth pursuing if calibration data shows Sauvola fails on a document class (per tenet #2, don't reach for NN unless deterministic proves insufficient).

## 3. Dedup (qc_phash)
- McKeown & Buchanan 2023, "Hamming distributions of popular perceptual hashing techniques" — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fsidi.2023.301509 — evaluates pHash/aHash/dHash robustness and Hamming-distance thresholds; most actionable paper for tuning qc_phash's dedup threshold.
- Meuschke et al 2018, "An Adaptive Image-based Plagiarism Detection Approach" — https://doi.org/10.1145/3197026.3197042 — image-based near-dup detection within documents specifically (not generic photos), closer analog to court-doc dedup than typical pHash literature.

## 4. Blank-page detection
Thin as standalone research topic — usually a deterministic heuristic (ink-pixel ratio/variance) inside scanning pipelines, which fits tenet #2 already. Closest hit: Wigington 2024, "Handheld Video Document Scanning: A Robust On-Device Model for Multi-Page Document Scanning" — https://doi.org/10.1145/3685650.3685662.

## 5. Tamil/Kannada OCR (Tesseract lang packs, tessdata_fast kan/tam)
- Hegghammer 2021, "OCR with Tesseract, Amazon Textract, and Google Document AI: a benchmarking experiment" — https://doi.org/10.1007/s42001-021-00149-1 — benchmarks Tesseract vs commercial engines under injected noise; useful if backend swap is ever justified per tenet #3.
- Gayathri Devi S et al 2022, "A Deep Learning Approach for Recognizing the Cursive Tamil Characters in Palm Leaf Manuscripts" — https://doi.org/10.1155/2022/3432330 (handwritten, lower priority — project corpus is printed).
- Hebbi & Mamatha 2023, "Comprehensive Dataset Building and Recognition of Isolated Handwritten Kannada Characters" — https://doi.org/10.47852/bonviewaia3202624 (dataset value only).

## 6. Document/OCR quality assessment (general QC heuristics)
- Alaei, Bui, Doermann et al 2023, "Document Image Quality Assessment: A Survey" — https://doi.org/10.1145/3606692 — best overview reference for the QC layer generally.
- Blando, Kanai, Nartker 1995, "Prediction of OCR accuracy using simple image features" — https://doi.org/10.1109/icdar.1995.599003 — deterministic feature-based OCR-quality prediction (not ML) — fits tenet #2 as a pre-OCR quality gate.
- Nikolaidou et al 2022, "A survey of historical document image datasets" — https://doi.org/10.1007/s10032-022-00405-8 — for expanding the calibration corpus if needed.

## Priority pick (most actionable, cheapest per tenet #1)
1. McKeown & Buchanan (pHash Hamming thresholds) — qc_phash tuning.
2. Shafait/Bukhari/Breuel (Sauvola param sensitivity) — directly tunes the just-shipped Sauvola binarization.
3. Blando et al (deterministic OCR-quality pre-gate) — new QC heuristic, no ML needed.

title: Deep-dive: Bukhari/Shafait/Breuel foreground-background guided Sauvola binarization (2009)
content:
Full-text read of https://doi.org/10.3217/jucs-015-18-3343 (PDF: https://zenodo.org/api/records/7001027/files/jucs_article_29563.pdf/content), picked as highest-impact paper from [[research-papers-algorithm-improvements]] because it directly targets the Sauvola binarization + A/B-testing work landed in commit 71a1753 (img to-bw --method sauvola + ocr-dump binarization A/B).

Sauvola threshold: t(x,y) = mu(x,y) * [1 + k*(sigma(x,y)/R - 1)], R=128 for 8-bit grayscale. No consensus on k: Sauvola/Sezgin use k=0.5, Badekas found k=0.34 best — paper shows k must be tuned per document collection (this validates the project's own A/B harness rather than hardcoding one k). Window size w is comparatively insensitive; k is the parameter that matters.

Tradeoff observed: small k (<=0.05) -> clean unbroken foreground strokes but noisy background; large k (>=0.2) -> clean background but broken characters. No single global k gets both.

Proposed fix: foreground/background-guided Sauvola — use two k values, k_r (small, ~0.02-0.05) near detected text ridges and k_nr (larger, ~0.2) elsewhere, via t(x,y) = mu(x,y)*[1 + k(x,y)*(sigma(x,y)/R - 1)] with k(x,y) selected per-pixel from a cheap foreground mask.

Results:
- OCR edit-distance (CBDAR-2007 dataset, ABBYY FineReader 9.0, 10 docs): Otsu 6.96% > tuned-Sauvola(w=15,k=0.15) 4.92% > guided-method 4.62% (best on 5/10 docs).
- Pixel F-measure (DIBCO-style low-res degraded docs, 4 images): Otsu 34.39% > tuned-Sauvola(w=15,k=0.05) 90.37% > guided-method 91.67%.
- Most relevant claim for production use: guided method is robust to the (k_r, k_nr) pair choice, while plain Sauvola's accuracy swings sharply with k — i.e. it reduces exactly the fragility the A/B harness is built to manage, not just peak accuracy.

Cost caveat: their foreground mask uses a multi-oriented multi-scale anisotropic Gaussian filter bank + Horn-Riley ridge detection — meaningfully slower than plain Sauvola, and the paper doesn't isolate how much of the accuracy gain requires that specific (expensive) mask vs. any reasonable foreground/background split.

Actionable next step for image-qc (fits tenet #1 delivery-over-cost, #3 cutting-not-bleeding-edge): before implementing the full anisotropic-Gaussian+ridge pipeline, try a much cheaper foreground proxy (local variance threshold, or morphological gradient/tophat mask) to pick k_r vs k_nr per-pixel, and A/B it in the existing ocr-dump harness against single-k Sauvola. Only escalate to the paper's full ridge-detection pipeline if the cheap proxy doesn't capture the robustness gain.

title: Real-corpus A/B result: guided Sauvola underperforms plain Sauvola on CBSL TND corpus
content:
Ran the sauvola_binarize_guided experiment (see [[sauvola-guided-binarization-deepdive]]) against a real 60-page stratified sample (every 16th page of 954) from ~/instadocs-refs/CBSL/TNDC33SA0008828/Colours (JPEG-compressed colour originals, 300dpi, ~2500x3600, Tamil court documents), via `qc-admin img to-bw --method {otsu,sauvola,guided}` + `img ocr-dump --lang tam`.

Environment notes: had to build qc_admin in --release (debug build was 16.8s/page, unusable); had to install system tesseract (`sudo pacman -S tesseract`, mirror was stale, needed `pacman -Syy` first) and point `QC_TESSERACT_DLL=/usr/lib/libtesseract.so.5` since this crate dlopens libtesseract at runtime (no tesseract-rs binding, no build-time link -- see qc_tesseract_ffi's own doc comment) and this Linux dev box has no bundled DLL the way the Windows build does; fetched tam.traineddata manually via curl since `mise run classify-assets` is Windows-only (PowerShell) and doesn't run here.

Results (60 pages):
- otsu: 5901 words total, 98.3 words/page, mean_conf 39.61
- sauvola (w=15,k=0.2): 7334 words total, 122.2 words/page, mean_conf 43.09
- guided (k_fg=0.05,k_bg=0.2,edge_frac=0.15): 6824 words total, 113.7 words/page, mean_conf 39.92

Guided is WORSE than plain sauvola here: -6.9% total words, -3.2 mean_conf points. Not an outlier artifact -- per-page breakdown is 29 pages worse / 25 better / 6 tied out of 60, avg word delta -8.5/page, i.e. a broad, systematic regression, not a couple of bad pages skewing the average.

This directly contradicts the synthetic test in gate.rs/lib.rs and the paper's premise. Most likely cause: the source images are JPEG-compressed (confirmed via `file`), and JPEG 8x8 DCT block-edge artifacts elevate local std broadly across the page -- exactly the kind of noise the cheap `std(x,y) >= edge_frac*r` proxy can't distinguish from a genuine text edge (unlike the paper's actual ridge-detection mask, which is shape-aware). Where the proxy misfires on JPEG noise, guided applies k_fg (small k) in effectively-background regions, thickening/adding noise there instead of correctly applying k_bg -- net effect likely worse than plain Sauvola's single, more conservative k=0.2 everywhere.

Verdict: do not adopt sauvola_binarize_guided over sauvola_binarize for this corpus/pipeline as-is. The cheap local-std proxy for the paper's ridge mask does not hold up on real (JPEG-sourced) scans -- confirms exactly the caveat already written into the function's own doc comment ("needs its own A/B pass... before it's trusted"). If revisiting: the most promising next step is denoising/deblocking (e.g. a small median or Gaussian pre-blur) before computing local std, to suppress JPEG-block-edge false positives, then re-run this same A/B -- not yet tried.

Branch `feat/sauvola-guided-binarization` is implemented, tested (synthetic unit tests still valid/pass), and this real-corpus result is now attached to it -- left uncommitted/unmerged pending this negative finding being seen.

title: Deep-dive: McKeown & Buchanan pHash Hamming-distance paper vs qc_phash's dedup_phash_distance=6
content:
Full-text read of arXiv:2212.08035 ("Hamming Distributions of Popular Perceptual Hashing Techniques", McKeown & Buchanan, DFRWS EU 2023), picked as next pick from [[research-papers-algorithm-improvements]] after the Sauvola deep-dive ([[sauvola-guided-binarization-deepdive]], [[guided-binarization-real-corpus-ab-result]]) came back negative.

qc_phash (rust/qc_phash/README.md) is a 64-bit DCT-based pHash -- the exact algorithm family the paper's `phash` row covers (ImageHash-library-compatible). Production default: `dedup_phash_distance=6` bits (tuning.json `use_rust_phash`), validated in-repo only for Rust-vs-Python implementation parity (4108-page CBSL corpus, 0.004-0.012% verdict divergence at thr=6), never against real duplicate/near-duplicate detection behavior.

Paper's phash-specific numbers (1M Flickr photos, normalized Hamming distance * 64 = bits):
- Inter-score (unrelated images): mean 0.4904 (31.4 bits), stdev 0.0649 (4.15 bits), RANGE 0.0938-0.8438 -- i.e. the closest two unrelated images got by chance in 50M pairwise comparisons was exactly 6 bits, matching qc_phash's current threshold exactly.
- Intra-score (same image after a content-preserving edit), mean bits (approx, *64): compression Q30 ~0.34 bits (83.9% exact match) -- inside threshold; scale 1.5x ~0.13 bits (94% exact) -- inside; crop 5% ~10.8 bits -- MISSES at thr=6; border (30px) ~17 bits -- MISSES; watermark ~7.85 bits -- usually MISSES; mirror(x-axis) ~31.4 bits -- statistically indistinguishable from random, pHash cannot detect mirroring at all for any threshold.

Interpretation for image-qc: threshold=6 is precision-biased (only catches identical-framing rescans/recompression) not recall-biased (misses cropped/bordered/stamped/mirrored duplicates). Also sits right at the paper's own observed random-collision floor for natural photos -- and document scans (repeated letterheads/stamps/templates) have less visual entropy than natural photos, so the false-positive-dedup risk is plausibly HIGHER here than in the paper's dataset, not lower. Given tenet #4 (operator override exists) and #6 (false-positive dedup silently treating two different real pages as duplicates is the more dangerous failure than a missed duplicate), staying precision-biased is a defensible choice, but the team should know that's what thr=6 actually buys -- it does not catch "same content, different framing/stamp."

Not yet done: an empirical version of this same analysis run against the actual CBSL corpus (~/instadocs-refs/CBSL/TNDC33SA0008828), computing real inter-page Hamming distances between genuinely different court-document pages, since the paper's numbers are for natural photos and court documents (shared letterheads/stamps/table layouts) are exactly the kind of low-entropy content the paper flags as a collision risk (their own finding: borders/watermarks bias distances toward similarity for most algorithms). This is the natural next real-corpus validation step, mirroring the Sauvola A/B methodology, using qc_phash's own existing `scripts/bench_phash_full.py` tooling -- offered to the user, not yet run.

title: Real-corpus finding: qc_phash dedup collides on recurring India Court Fee stamp-paper pages
content:
Empirical follow-up to [[phash-hamming-threshold-deepdive]], answering the open question there (paper's numbers are for natural photos; do real templated court documents cluster more dangerously?). Built `qc-admin img phash-scan <dir> [--threshold N] [--top N]` (new subcommand, rust/qc_admin/src/imgcmd.rs, branch `diag/phash-corpus-hamming-check`, not yet committed) -- a from-scratch reimplementation of qc_phash's exact algorithm (32x32 downsample -> DCT2D top-left 8x8 -> median -> MSB-first pack), using `image::imageops::resize(Lanczos3)` instead of qc_phash's SIMD fast_image_resize (same divergence the project's own qc_phash README already accepts between its own two backends -- not a new source of uncertainty). Couldn't link qc_phash itself: it's `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` with pyo3 `extension-module`, dlopen-only, not a normal Rust dependency.

Ran on the full 954-page ~/instadocs-refs/CBSL/TNDC33SA0008828/Colours corpus (same corpus as [[guided-binarization-real-corpus-ab-result]]):
- 454,581 total page pairs; 2716 pairs (0.60%) land at-or-below the production `dedup_phash_distance=6` default -- vs. the paper's natural-photo baseline where the CLOSEST unrelated-image pair in 50M comparisons was exactly 6 bits (a rare boundary case there, routine here).
- 92 pairs are EXACT hash collisions (distance=0), clustering into groups of genuinely different pages (e.g. one cluster of 9 pages, one of 6, several of 3-4).

Visually verified two flagged distance-0 pairs (page 65 vs page 97, via PIL thumbnail conversion + Read) -- confirmed real, DIFFERENT documents: both are "India Court Fee Rs.100" stamp-paper sheets (standard Indian legal stamp paper, one per court filing/exhibit), same dominant printed template graphic, but different handwritten case numbers/annotations (e.g. "59" vs "91", different plaintiff/defendant text). The pHash's coarse 8x8-DCT low-frequency encoding captures the large identical printed stamp graphic and loses the fine handwritten differences entirely -- exactly the collision risk the McKeown/Buchanan paper predicts for low-entropy/templated content, now confirmed on this project's actual document type.

Severity check: `rust/qc_worker/src/dedup.rs` shows dedup runs unconditionally by default (disable only via `QC_DEDUP=0`), two-stage (blake3 exact prefilter, then phash near-dup against all prior pages WITHIN THE SAME RUN). Crucially NON-destructive: `DedupState::check` only returns a `DupHit` -> `FLAG_DUPLICATE` row (image_qc/db/repositories/flags.py) surfaced in `DuplicateReviewDialog` (image_qc/ui/dialogs/duplicates.py) for operator confirm/reject ("Keep Both"). So this is NOT a silent data-loss risk (tenet #6 upheld) -- it's an operator-review-burden problem: a case file full of stamp-paper-affixed exhibits (common pattern for Indian court filings) would generate a large number of false-positive duplicate-review flags that are all genuinely different pages, potentially eroding operator trust in the duplicate-review panel ("it always flags the stamp papers, I just click Keep Both") -- exactly the kind of alert-fatigue failure mode that undermines tenet #4's human-in-the-loop design if it happens often enough.

Not yet done / open follow-up: DedupState.check matches against "the first prior page within range" in seen-order, not exhaustive nearest-neighbor, so actual production flag count per case would be roughly (cluster_size - 1) per stamp-paper cluster rather than the full pairwise count -- still likely dozens of flags on a stamp-paper-heavy case, but this wasn't precisely measured (would need to replay DedupState's exact sequential logic over the real corpus, not just compute the raw pairwise histogram). No fix implemented or proposed yet -- worth a follow-up conversation on whether a mitigation is warranted (e.g. excluding a known-template region from the hash, or accepting the review burden as-is since it's non-destructive).

title: agentflare code impact — implemented on task/21
content: Added `agentflare code impact <path> [--stdin] [--json]` (new `code` command domain). src/code/workspace_graph.rs parses `cargo metadata` into a crate graph (manifest_dir, own test/bench/example targets, transitive reverse-dependents incl dev-deps); src/code/confirm.rs confirms cross-crate refs via `lean-ctx grep` with a built-in `regex` fallback (skips target/, honours .gitignore); src/code/mod.rs impact_for_path composes them (own tests always count; cross-crate candidates only when a `use <crate_ident>::` hit). Regression test tests/code_impact_test.rs builds a 2-crate temp workspace with two same-named supervisor.rs files — resolver does not conflate them. Also added a minimal `[lib]` target (src/lib.rs) since the root crate was bin-only; needed for `cargo test --test code_impact_test` to `use agentflare::code`. Commits: a3c3e73 (WorkspaceGraph), 44f6c81 (confirm), 9cec5f8 (impact_for_path), ef9dde3 (CLI). Deviations from plan: (1) added `.gitignore` (target) to the fallback-scan test fixture so lean-ctx grep and the built-in scan agree on the "skip target/" expectation (lean-ctx grep includes target/ without one); (2) `cargo fmt` reorders `mod code;` after `mod coaching;` (alphabetical); (3) ImpactReport/ImpactHit derive Debug (test .unwrap_err() requires it). Symbol-name mode deferred per plan.

title: [opencode] quota::decide() tier precedence
content: decide() runs 6 precedence tiers: 1 health-gate (high-sev vent→Ask, low/med under SELF_REPAIR_CAP=3→SelfRepair, at cap→Ask), 2 operator-gate (Gated lifecycle→Ask), 3 evidence-wait (started sibling with stale claim→Wait), 4 focus-wait (live foreign claim on item→Wait), 5 eligibility (unconfirmed agent→StayQuiet), 6 compute-quota stub (v1 always passes). Ungrouped items skip tiers 1-4; malformed goal JSON fails closed to Ask.

Build wrapper dying (MCP shell timeout) leaves cargo done but bundle unfinished — re-run the script, deps cached so it's fast.

title: Dashboard PR #255 MERGED to master (Phases 0–2)
content:
**PR #255 (read-only dashboard, Phases 0–2) is MERGED to master** as squash commit `6cda051` (2026-07-18). Also merged same session: **PR #252** (ui-module cliclack consolidation) = squash `94c6c4a`.

**To get #255 mergeable this session:**
- Resolved a Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock conflict with master (master had added crate `agentflare-store` + relicensed MIT→Apache-2.0). Cargo.toml = pure union of deps; kept master's members/license.
- **Gotcha:** a first `cargo update --offline` DOWNGRADED `crossbeam-epoch` 0.9.20→0.9.18, reintroducing RUSTSEC-2026-0204 → `cargo audit` CI failed. Fix: `git checkout origin/master -- Cargo.lock` then `cargo build` (online) to add only the new deps without disturbing master's patched pins. Lesson: reconcile lockfiles ONLINE, never offline.
- The full `ci.yml` (build×3/clippy/fmt/cargo-deny) had never gated this branch before; on first real run **fmt + clippy failed**. `cargo fmt` fixed formatting; clippy `-D warnings` flagged dead `dashboard::data::live_snapshot_json` (orphaned by the SSE broadcast refactor — producer calls `snapshot_json` directly). Deleted the fn + its unit test. Dashboard tests now 11 (was 12).

**#252 fix:** its only blocker was a non-conventional PR title (`ui-module:` not a valid type for the amannn/action-semantic-pull-request check added in #250). Retitled to `refactor:` + `gh pr update-branch` (it was BEHIND). Repo requires branches up-to-date + conventional PR titles; merge method = SQUASH.

**Still NOT done:** Phase 3 (Gateway/Memory/Channels) — plan asset on AGENTFLARE-1. Claims/Cost views still local-only, not synced to claude.ai/design project 0196b412-a535-482d-a0c1-6e0eb7a8c3d4.
